COORDINATOR-VERIFIED: carries exactly the lab pair (lab.sqlite 6242304->6311936, web/data/lab.json), nothing of a peer; grid.csv still byte-identical to 661870d. Headline is a NEGATIVE result answering R2: the single-name brake does not move the fall. Full verdict/insight report pending. | VERDICT LANDED 01efde8 "M0155 -- the brake fires on names the book does not own" (two dated docs files; grid.csv re-verified byte-identical to 661870d). THE RESULT: every arm spring-2006 fall is 21.83%% -- identical to the unbraked book to four decimals -- and five of six arms are identical on every era column on BOTH histories. Control reproduces its recorded trial (daily fall, funded return, trade count) to six digits, and the seven recorded widths were re-measured here under ONE convention so the two are directly comparable, which also resolves the month-end convention problem phase 3 found earlier. THE MECHANISM, the part worth keeping: the brake fires on 77%% of monthly decisions and named 820 names in twenty years, OF WHICH THE BOOK HELD ELEVEN. In spring 2006 it named thirty-six and held NONE. The book ranks on a year of momentum and buys the top twenty; a name two standard deviations behind the index over a quarter is already out of that twenty. The two screens select nearly disjoint sets, so the brake spends its life reading names the book does not own. This is why it does nothing -- a far more useful answer than it failed, and it closes R2 with a mechanism rather than a null.

Texture: against two of the four failed books the control reads 0.359/0.343 and the drawdown-braked arms 0.625/0.631 -- account-reading brakes cost about half the distance to the line, market-reading brakes cost all of it. COST: every brake works and every one is paid out of the return. Worst fall 68.7%->19.3-33.2%; funded return 9.9%->5.9-9.2% vs SPY TR 7.2%. A recovery cost not a crash cost -- the drawdown brake turned a 23%/yr 2009-2015 stretch into 12.9%/yr. All six failed DSR>=0.90 (0.51-0.67 at N=95), 0 of 4 folds. phases.note: M0148 REJECTED DIRECTION, the rare clean kind -- lost return AND safety at once, nothing to trade off. wait none 11.3%/20.4%/+4.1 SPY lead; 1 check 10.2/20.4/+3.0; 2 checks 9.8/25.3/+2.6; 3 checks 9.0/31.6/+1.8; 3 sell-only 10.0/31.4/+2.9. Monotone decay in return and the worst fall goes the WRONG way, 20->32%. A brake that deepens the drawdown is not a brake. ANCHOR HELD IN THE RECORDED PATH, not just the pre-check: M0148-K0 vs trial n=467 identical to the digit on start, end, trades 575, max_drawdown, cagr, profit_factor, exposure, turnover. ONLY dsr differs (0.943236881080622 vs M0143's 0.941320611624543) and that is CORRECT not a miss -- DSR is scored at its run-date N and N moved since M0143 ran. NOT A NULL: the cool-off genuinely bound, 8/14/24/15 refused moves over 238 checks, turnover 5.37->5.03, switch 31 changes of mind -> 23. The idea got a real chance and was refused on its merits. WHERE THE MONEY WENT -- 2008: the book beat the market by 35.7% that year with the switch free and by only 27-28% in every version that made it wait. The suppressed flips were not whipsaw, they were the exit the switch exists for; at three checks it was blocked from selling in May/June/July 2008 and from buying back through three straight months of the 2003 recovery. Chop years never improved: 2009-2015 reads -0.5% with no lock and -1.4/-0.6/-1.0/-0.0 with it, AND the binds do not match the story -- clustered in 2011 and early 2012, none in 2010, none in 2015, said so in the verdict rather than letting the three-year framing stand.
